records: What did David do after defeating the Amalekites?
David returned from defeating the Amalekites and remained in Ziklag for two days without receiving any news of the battle between the Philistines and Israelites.
On the third day, who came to David from Saul’s camp?
On the third day, a man with his clothes torn and with dirt on his head came to David.
What did the young man say about Saul and Jonathan?
The young man said that Saul and his son Jonathan were killed.
Where did the young man say he found Saul?
The young man said he was on Mount Gilboa, and Saul was there leaning on his spear.
What did the young man say Saul asked him to do?
The young man said Saul asked him to stand over him and kill him.
Why did Saul ask the young Amalekite man to kill him?
Saul asked the young Amalekite man to kill him because great agony had seized him, but his life was still in him.
After the young man killed Saul, what did he take from Saul?
The young man took the crown that was on Saul’s head and the band that was on his arm.
What did David and his men do when they heard about the deaths of Saul and Jonathan?
David and his men tore their clothes, and they mourned, wept, and fasted until evening.
For whom else were David and his men mourning?
David and his men also mourned for the people of Yahweh and for the house of Israel, because they had fallen by the sword.
Why did David have the young Amalekite man killed?
David had the young Amalekite man killed because the man’s own words testified that he had killed Yahweh’s anointed.
Why did David have the young Amalekite man killed?
David had the young Amalekite man killed because the man’s own words testified that he had killed Yahweh’s anointed.
Where is the funeral song that David sang for Saul and Jonathan written?
The song is written in the Book of Jashar.
What was slain on Israel’s high places?
The splendor of Israel was slain there.
Why did David not want the news of the defeat proclaimed in Gath or Ashkelon?
He did not want the daughters of the Philistines to rejoice or triumph.
Where does the shield of the Saul, the mighty king, remain?
The shield of the mighty king remains on ground on Mount Gilboa.
What did Saul do for the daughters of Israel?
He made Israel a safe and prosperous place in which they had beautiful scarlet clothes and expensive jewelry and gold ornaments to wear.
How did David describe his love for Jonathan?
David said Jonathan’s love for him was more wonderful than the love of women.
What did David ask Yahweh, and what was the reply?
David asked if he should go up to one of the cities of Judah, and Yahweh told him to go up.
When David inquired further, to which city did Yahweh tell David to go?
Yahweh told David to go to Hebron.
Who went up with David to Hebron?
David went up to Hebron with his two wives, Ahinoam and Abigail, and all his men and their families.
What did the men of Judah do when they came to David?
The men of Judah came and anointed David as king over the house of Judah.
What did Abner do with Ishbosheth, the son of Saul?
Abner took Ishbosheth to Mahanaim and made him king of all the territory that would later be the northern kingdom of Israel.
Abner was the son of Ner and the commander of Saul’s army.
How long was David king in Hebron over the house of Judah?
David was king in Hebron over the house of Judah for seven years and six months.
Where did Joab’s men and Abner’s men meet?
They met near the large pool of Gibeon, staying on opposite sides of the pool.
How many young men fought before Joab and Abner?
Twelve men from Benjamin for Ishbosheth and twelve men from David’s soldiers fought.
Who won the battle that day?
The soldiers of David defeated Abner and the soldiers from the other tribes of Israel.
Which son of Zeruiah pursued Abner?
How did Abner try to convince Asahel to stop pursuing him?
Abner warned Asahel that if he had to strike him down, he could never again have a peaceful relationship with Asahel’s brother Joab.
What happened to Asahel when he refused to stop pursuing Abner?
Abner struck him in the stomach with the butt end of his spear, and the spear went right through his stomach and came out of his back, so Asahel fell and died there.
To what location did Joab and Abishai pursue Abner?
Joab and Abishai pursued Abner to the hill of Ammah, which is near Giah on the way to the wilderness of Gibeon.
What did Abner say to stop Joab from pursuing him?

Abner called out to Joab that they should not continue this deadly battle any longer. He told Joab to realize that if they continue fighting, many people will suffer great harm. He said that they are all Israelites, and asked Joab to please tell his soldiers right now to stop chasing Abner and his soldiers.
Where did Abner and his men travel?
Abner and his men marched back to Mahanaim.
Where did Joab and his men travel?
Joab and his men traveled to Hebron to bury Asahel’s body in the tomb of his father at Bethlehem. Then they marched all night, going back to Hebron, their home.
In the war between the house of Saul and the house of David, who grew stronger and who grew weaker?
The house of David grew stronger, and the house of Saul grew weaker.
Who were David’s first three sons born to him in Hebron?
Amnon, Chileab, and Absalom were the first three sons born to David in Hebron.
What did Ishbosheth accuse Abner of doing?
Ishbosheth accused Abner of doing something wrong by having sexual relations with his father Saul’s concubine.
After Ishbosheth’s accusation, what did Abner swear he would do?
Abner swore that he would transfer the kingdom from Saul’s house to David and establish David’s throne over all Israel and Judah.
What was David’s one condition for making a covenant with Abner?
Abner had to bring his wife Michal, Saul’s daughter, when he came to see David.
What price had David paid for Michal to be his wife?
David had paid the price of 100 Philistine foreskins for Michal.
What did Abner tell the elders of Israel to do?

Abner told the elders to make David their king, since Yahweh spoke about David, saying that by the hand of his servant David my servant, he would save his people Israel from the hand of the Philistines and from the hand of all of their enemies.
What did David do for Abner when Abner and his twenty men arrived in Hebron?
David made a feast for Abner and his men.
What did Abner tell David he planned to do?
Abner said he would gather all of Israel to David so they could make a covenant with him, and so David could reign over all that he desired.
How did David and Abner part ways?
David sent Abner away, and he went in peace.
What did Joab accuse Abner of doing?
Joab accused Abner of coming to deceive David and to learn all about his plans.
What did Joab do after he had Abner brought back to Hebron?
To avenge the death of his brother Asahel, Joab took Abner aside to the middle of the gate and struck him in the stomach, and he died.
Why did David curse Joab for murdering Abner?
Joab and Abishai his brother had murdered Abner because he had killed Asahel their brother at Gibeon in the battle. They should not have taken revenge.
After Joab killed Abner, what curse did David pronounce on Joab’s family?

David pronounced a curse that the guilt for Abner’s blood would be on Joab and his father’s house forever. He asked that there will always be someone in Joab’s family who has sores or who is a leper or who cannot walk without a crutch or who dies in battle or who does not have enough food to eat.
What did David tell Joab and all the people with him to do?
David told them to tear their clothes, put on sackcloth, and mourn for Abner.
What did David swear when the people urged him to eat?
David swore an oath that he would not taste bread or anything else for the rest of this day.
What did all the people of Israel understand from David’s mourning for Abner?
They understood that the king had not wanted Joab to kill Abner.
What did the king say to his servants about Abner?
The king told his servants that a commander and a great man had fallen that day in Israel.
What did David hope for the sons of Zeruiah?
David hoped that Yahweh would repay the evildoer according to his evil.
What caused Ishbosheth’s hands to become weak?
When Ishbosheth heard that Abner was dead in Hebron, his hands became weak.
What were the names of two of Ishbosheth’s commanders?
The names of two of his commanders were Baanah and Rechab.
What was the name of Jonathan’s son who was crippled in his feet?
The name of Jonathan’s son who was crippled in his feet was Mephibosheth.
How did Rechab and Baanah get into Ishbosheth’s house?
They went into the middle of the house as if they were getting wheat.
What did Rechab and Baanah do once they were inside Ishbosheth’s house?
They went to his private bedroom and they stabbed and killed him as he was lying asleep on his bed, and then they removed his head.
Where did Rechab and Baanah go after they killed Ishbosheth?
They brought the head of Ishbosheth to David at Hebron.
What did David say about Rechab and Baanah?
David said they were wicked men who had murdered a righteous man in his own house on his bed.
On David’s orders, what did the young men do to Rechab and Baanah?
The young men killed Rechab and Baanah, cut off their hands and feet, and hung them beside the pool at Hebron.
What did David have done with the head of Ishbosheth?
David had the head of Ishbosheth buried in Abner’s grave in Hebron.
What did the tribes of Israel say Yahweh had promised David?
They said Yahweh had promised that David would shepherd his people Israel and become their ruler.
Who came to Hebron, made a covenant with David, and anointed him king over Israel?
All the elders of Israel came to Hebron, made a covenant with David, and anointed him king over Israel.
How many years did David reign in Jerusalem over all Israel and Judah?
David reigned in Jerusalem for 33 years over all Israel and Judah.
By what other names was Jerusalem called?
The stronghold of Zion was also called the City of David.
From whom did David capture the stronghold of Zion?
David captured the stronghold of Zion from the Jebusites.
Why did David become greater and greater?
David became greater and greater because Yahweh, the God of Armies, was with him.
What did Hiram, king of Tyre, send to David?
Hiram sent messengers, cedar trees, carpenters, and stonemasons to David to build a house for David.
How many sons were born to David in Jerusalem?
Eleven sons were born to David in Jerusalem.
What did the Philistines do when they heard that David had been anointed king over Israel?
When the Philistines heard David had been anointed king, they marched toward Jerusalem to try to capture David.
What did Yahweh tell David when David asked if he should attack the Philistines?
Yahweh told David to go up because he would definitely enable David’s army to defeat them.
Where did David attack the Philistines, and what was the outcome?
David attacked the Philistines at Baal Perazim and defeated them there.
When the Philistines came up a second time, how did Yahweh tell David to attack them?
Yahweh told David not to go up to attack them from the front, but to circle around behind them and attack from opposite the balsam trees.
What sound did Yahweh tell David to listen for before attacking the Philistines?
Yahweh told David to attack when he heard the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees.
What was David’s response to Yahweh’s command?
David did just as Yahweh had commanded him.
What was the outcome of this battle against the Philistines?
David’s soldiers defeated the Philistine soldiers and chased them from the city of Geba all the way west to the city of Gezer.
Why did David gather all the chosen men of Israel?
David gathered the chosen men of Israel to bring up the Box of God from Baalah of Judah.
On what did they set the Box of God?
They set the Box of God on a new cart pulled by two oxen.
Who was guiding the new cart?
Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, were guiding the new cart.
What happened at the threshing floor of Nacon?
The oxen stumbled, and Uzzah reached out to steady the Box of God.
What did God do in response to Uzzah’s action?
God became angry and struck Uzzah for his fault, and Uzzah died there by the Box of God.
How did David feel about what Yahweh had done to Uzzah?

David was angry because Yahweh had broken out against Uzzah. Then David became afraid of Yahweh, and he said that it was too dangerous for him to try to bring the sacred chest to where he lived in Jerusalem.
What did David do with the Box of God after Uzzah died?
David decided not to bring the sacred chest to the City of David. Instead, he had the people take it into the house of Obed Edom, there by the road.
Why did David bring the Box of God from Obed Edom’s house to the City of David?
David brought it because he was told that Yahweh had blessed the house of Obed Edom because of the Box of God.
What did David do as the Box of God was being brought up?
As the Box of God was being brought up, David, wearing a linen ephod, danced before Yahweh with all his strength.
What was Michal’s response when she saw King David leaping and dancing before Yahweh?
When Michal saw King David leaping and dancing before Yahweh, she despised him in her heart.
After the Box of Yahweh was set in its place, what offerings did David make to Yahweh?
David offered burnt offerings and peace offerings to Yahweh.
What did David distribute to all the people?
He distributed a cake of bread, a date cake, and a raisin cake to each person.
What did Michal say to David when he returned home?
She sarcastically asked how the king of Israel had honored himself by uncovering himself before the eyes of his servants’ female servants, like a worthless person.
What was David’s response to Michal’s rebuke?
David said that he celebrated before Yahweh, who chose him as leader. He said he would humble himself even more, and that the female servants would honor him.
Yahweh gave David rest from all his surrounding enemies.
What did the king say to Nathan the prophet?
The king said to Nathan that he was living in a house of cedar, but the Box of God was dwelling in a tent.
What did Nathan tell David before the word of Yahweh came to him?
Nathan told David to do all that was in his heart, because Yahweh was with him.
What question did Yahweh ask about the leaders of Israel?
Yahweh asked if he had ever commanded one of the leaders of Israel to build him a house of cedars.
What did Yahweh say he had done for David?
Yahweh said he took David from the pasture to be ruler over Israel, had been with him everywhere, and had cut off all his enemies from before him.
What did Yahweh say he was going to do for Israel?
Yahweh said he had established a place for them and will plant them so they could live in their own place and not be afflicted by wicked people anymore.
Who did Yahweh say would build a house for his name?
Yahweh said he would raise up David’s own offspring after him, and that offspring would build a house for his name.
What did Yahweh say about David’s house and kingdom?
Yahweh said David’s descendants would continually rule the kingdom of Israel after him.
After Nathan told David all the words Yahweh had said, what did David do?
David went in and sat before Yahweh and prayed to him.
After hearing the prophecy, what did David say about Yahweh?
David said that Yahweh knew his servant so well.
Why did David say Yahweh had done this great thing and revealed it to him?
David said Yahweh had done it for the sake of his word and according to his own heart.
Why did God go to redeem Israel?
God redeemed Israel to make them a people for himself and to make a name for himself.
Why did David say he had been bold enough to pray like this to Yahweh?
David said he found the heart to pray because Yahweh had revealed that he would build a house for David.
What did David say about Yahweh’s words?
David said that Yahweh’s words are true.
What did David ask Yahweh to do?
David asked Yahweh to be pleased to bless his house so that it would continue forever before him.
What did David gain by attacking and subduing the Philistines?
They captured Metheg Ammah and made the Philistines subject to the Israelites.
How did David decide which Moabite soldiers would live or die?
He made them lie on the ground and measured them with a rope, measuring two rope lengths to be killed and one full rope length to be kept alive.
What happened to the Moabites who were left alive?
The rest of the Moabites had to accept David as their ruler. Every year they had to give him the payment that he demanded.
What did David capture from Hadadezer?
David captured from him 1,700 horsemen and 20,000 men on foot.
What did David do to the Arameans of Damascus when they came to help Hadadezer?
David struck 22,000 men among the Arameans.
Each time David led his soldiers into battle, Yahweh enabled them to win victories over their enemies.
What did Toi, king of Hamath, do when he heard that David had defeated Hadadezer’s army?
Toi sent his son Joram to greet and bless David, and Joram brought vessels of silver, gold, and bronze.
What did David do with the silver and gold from the nations he had subdued?
David consecrated the silver and gold to Yahweh.
Where did David strike the Arameans?
David killed 18,000 Arameans in the Valley of Salt.
What did David do for all his people?
David did justice and righteousness for all his people.
How did David’s sons serve his kingdom?
Why did David want to show covenant faithfulness to anyone left in Saul’s house?
David wanted to show covenant faithfulness for the sake of Jonathan.
How did Ziba answer the king when he was asked if anyone was left in Saul’s house?
Ziba told the king that one son of Jonathan was still alive but not able to walk.
Who was left in Saul’s house?
Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, was left.
What kindness did David show Mephibosheth for Jonathan’s sake?
David restored to Mephibosheth all the land of his grandfather Saul, and he had Mephibosheth eat meals with his family continually.
What did David tell Ziba to do for Mephibosheth?
David told Ziba that he, his sons, and his servants were to work the land for Mephibosheth and bring in the harvest.
Where did Mephibosheth live after David showed him kindness?
Mephibosheth lived in Jerusalem because he ate meals with David’s family in the palace.
What physical problem did Mephibosheth have?
Mephibosheth was lame in both of his feet.
Who became king of the Ammonites after the former king died?
Hanun his son became the new king.
How did David show kindness to Hanun?
David sent his servants to console Hanun concerning the death of his father.
What did the Ammonite commanders say about David’s show of kindness to Hanun?
The commanders told Hanun that David had sent his servants to explore the city in order to spy on it and overthrow it.
What did Hanun do to David’s servants?

He commanded his soldiers to seize David’s officials and insult them by shaving off one side of their beards and cut off the lower part of their robes so that their buttocks would show. Then he sent them back to Israel.
Where did the Ammonites and their hired soldiers position themselves for battle?
The Ammonites formed a battle line at their city gate, while their hired soldiers from Aram, Tob, and Maacah were by themselves in the field.
Why did the Ammonites hire soldiers from other nations?
The Ammonites hired soldiers because they saw that they had greatly insulted David.
What did David do when he heard that the Ammonites had hired soldiers?
When David heard of it, he sent Joab and all the army of mighty men to fight against them.
How did Joab prepare for the battle?
Joab chose some of the best men of Israel and arrayed them to meet the Arameans, and he put the rest of the people in the hand of his brother Abishai to meet the Ammonites.
What did the Ammonites do when they saw that the Arameans had fled from Joab?
When the Ammonites saw that the Arameans had fled, they also fled from Abishai and went into the city.
What did the Arameans do when they saw they had been defeated by Israel?
The Arameans gathered themselves together again at Helam, and Hadadezer sent for many troops from Aramean kingdoms beyond the Euphrates River.
What did David do when he heard that the Arameans had gathered again?
David gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan, and came toward Helam to fight the Arameans.
What did all the kings who were servants of Hadadezer do when they saw they were defeated by Israel?
They made peace with Israel and served them. The Arameans would not help the Ammonites anymore after that, because they were afraid of Israel.
When did kings normally go out to war?
Kings normally went out to war at the return of the year, in the spring.
Where was King David at this time?
David sent out his commander Joab with his officers and the rest of the Israelite army, but David himself stayed in Jerusalem.
Who did David see one evening when he was walking on the roof of his palace?
David saw a very beautiful woman bathing, and her name was Bathsheba.
Bathsheba’s husband was Uriah the Hittite.
What did David do with Bathsheba?
David sent for her, he had sexual relations with her, and she became pregnant.
After David found out Bathsheba was pregnant, what did he do?
He told Joab to send Uriah the Hittite to him.
When Uriah came to David, what did David try to get him to do?
David tried to get Uriah to go down to his house and relax for a while.
What did Uriah do after David told him to go to his house?
Uriah did not go to his house, but instead slept at the entrance of the king’s house with all the servants of his master.
Why did Uriah say he would not go to his own house?
Uriah said he would never go to his house to eat, drink, and lie with his wife while the Box, Israel, and Judah were dwelling in tents, and Joab and his men were camping in the open field.
What did David’s letter to Joab say?
The letter said to put Uriah in the front of the strongest battle and then to retreat from him so he would be struck and die.
What did Joab think might happen when his messenger brought news of the war to David?
Joab thought David might become angry because he had allowed the Ammonites to kill some of his soldiers.
What news did Joab think David might be angry about?
Joab thought David might be angry that soldiers got so close to the city to fight because the Ammonite soldiers would shoot arrows at them from the top of the city wall.
What did Joab tell the messenger to say if David got angry?
Joab told the messenger to say that his servant Uriah the Hittite was also dead.
What did David tell the messenger to say to Joab?

David told the messenger to encourage Joab by telling him to not feel badly since no one ever knows who might die in a battle. David advised him to strengthen his battle against the city and destroy it.
What did Uriah’s wife do when she heard that her husband was dead?
When she heard her husband was dead, she mourned for him.
After her mourning passed, David sent for her, and she became his wife, and she bore him a son.
Who was displeased with what David had done?
Yahweh was very displeased with what David had done.
The story was about a rich man with many flocks and herds and a poor man who had only one little ewe lamb that was like a daughter to him.
Why did Nathan go to David?
Nathan went to David because Yahweh sent him.
What did the rich man do with the poor man’s lamb?
When a traveler came to the rich man, he took the poor man’s lamb and prepared it as a meal for his guest.
What was David’s reaction to Nathan’s story?
David was very angry and said that he wanted to execute the man who did that.
What did Nathan tell David after David reacted in anger?
Nathan told David, “You are the man.”
What did Yahweh say David had done?

Yahweh said David had struck Uriah the Hittite with the sword, had taken his wife to be his own wife, and had murdered him with the sword of the Ammonites. Yahweh said that David did not take seriously what he commanded when he said that his people must not commit adultery or murder. David did things that Yahweh considers to be very evil!
What did Yahweh say would happen because David despised him and took Uriah’s wife?

Yahweh said that he would make someone from David’s own family cause disaster for him. Yahweh would take David’s wives away from him and give them to that person instead. He will have sexual relations with them in public.
After he confessed his sin, what did Nathan say would happen to David?
Nathan told David that Yahweh had taken away his sin and that he would not die.
What did Nathan say would happen to the son born to David?
Nathan said that because David had shown great contempt for Yahweh by doing this, the son born to him would surely die.
What did David do when the child was very sick?
David prayed to God that the child would not die, fasted, and went in and slept on the floor of his room.
The child died on the seventh day.
What did David do once he knew the child was dead?
David arose from the ground, washed and anointed himself, changed his clothes, and went to the house of Yahweh and prostrated himself. Then he asked his servants for food and he ate it.
Why did David stop fasting after the child died?
David reasoned that there was no reason to fast since he could not bring the child back again.
Why did Yahweh send word through Nathan to name the new son Jedidiah?
Yahweh said to name him Jedidiah because of Yahweh.
Against whom was Joab fighting at this time?
Joab was fighting against Rabbah of the sons of Ammon.
Why did Joab tell David to gather the rest of the army and capture the city?
Joab did not want to capture the city himself, because if he did, it would renamed to honor him and not King David.
What did David make the people of Rabbah do after he captured the city?
David brought out the people and set them to work with saws, iron picks, and iron axes. David’s troops also forced them to make bricks.
To whom was Amnon, the son of David, attracted?
Amnon loved his beautiful half-sister Tamar, who was the sister of Absalom.
How did Amnon respond when Jonadab asked him why he was so weak?
Amnon told Jonadab that he loved Tamar, his brother Absalom’s sister.
What did Amnon do to get to see Tamar?
Amnon pretended to be sick, and when David came to see him, he asked David to let Tamar come and make food for him so he could eat from her hand.
What did Amnon do when Tamar came to feed him?
When Tamar came to feed him, he seized her and told her to come and lie with him.
What did Amnon do when Tamar begged him not to force her?
He refused to do what she said he should do. He was stronger than she was, so he forcibly had sexual relations with her.
How did Amnon feel toward Tamar after he raped her?
Amnon hated her with a very great hatred that was greater than the love with which he had loved her.
What did Amnon command Tamar to do?
What did Amnon order his servant to do?
He ordered his servant to send Tamar outside and to lock the door behind her.
What did Tamar do after she was put out of Amnon’s room?
Tamar tore the long robe that she was wearing. She put ashes on her head, and she put her hand on her head. As she went away, she kept screaming.
What was King David’s response when he heard about these things?
When King David heard all these things, it made him very angry, but he did nothing about it.
How did Absalom feel toward Amnon after he raped Tamar?
Absalom hated Amnon because he had humbled his sister Tamar.
Whom did Absalom invite to visit him at Baal Hazor?
Absalom invited the king and all the king’s sons to visit him.
What did the king say in response to Absalom’s invitation?
The king said they should not all go because they would be a heavy burden to Absalom.
What did David say when Absalom asked him to let Amnon go with them?
But the king replied, “You do not need to invite him to the celebration either.”
Absalom urged David, so he sent Amnon and all the king’s sons with him.
What did Absalom command his servants to do to Amnon?
Absalom commanded his servants to kill Amnon when Amnon began to be drunk with wine.
What did the king’s sons do after Absalom’s servants killed Amnon?
All the king’s sons arose, and they got onto their mules and escaped by riding away fast.
What was the first news David heard about the incident?
The first report to David said that Absalom had killed all the king’s sons and not one was still alive.
What did Jonadab say had happened and why?
Jonadab said that only Amnon is dead. Absalom has been determined to kill him ever since the day that Amnon raped his sister Tamar.
Where did Absalom go after having Amnon killed?
Absalom fled to Talmai, the son of Ammihud, king of Geshur.
How long was Absalom in Geshur?
Absalom was in Geshur for three years.
What did King David intend to do?
King David had intended to attack Absalom and punish him for killing Amnon.
What did Joab do when he knew the king’s heart was against Absalom?
Joab sent to Tekoa and brought a wise woman from there to act as if she had been in mourning for a long time.
What did Joab want the wise woman to do?
Joab wanted the wise woman to pretend to be a mourner and to go speak to the king the words Joab told her to say.
When the wise woman went to the king, whom did she say she was?
The wise woman told the king she was a widow.
What did the wise woman tell the king her two sons had done?
She told the king that her two sons fought in a field, and one struck the other and killed him.
What did the wise woman tell the king she was afraid would happen to her remaining son?
She said she was afraid the whole clan would kill her remaining son, destroying her heir and leaving no descendants to preserve her family’s name.
Why did the wise woman ask the king to remember Yahweh his God?
She asked the king to remember Yahweh so that the avenger of blood would not destroy her son.
Who did the king swear by when he told the woman that not one hair of her son would fall to the ground?
The king swore by the life of Yahweh.
Why did the woman say the king had been doing the wrong thing?
The woman said the king was acting badly because he had not brought back his own banished son.
What did the woman say God does instead of taking away life?
She said that God forgives people who have sinned against him so that they can once more be in a good relationship with him.
Why did the woman say she came to speak to the king?
She said she came because the people had frightened her, and she hoped the king would listen and deliver her.
What did the woman say about the king?
She said that what the king says will comfort her, because he is like an angel of God, and he knows how to determine what is right and what is wrong.
What did the king ask the woman?
The king asked the woman if Joab arranged for her to do all this.
Why did Joab have the woman go to the king?
Joab did that to try to get David to feel differently about this matter.
What did Joab do when the king told him to bring Absalom back?
Joab lay facedown on the ground in honor and gratitude to the king.
What instructions did the king give about Absalom?
The king said that Absalom could return to his own house but could go and speak with the king.
What was notable about Absalom’s appearance?
He was so handsome that people throughout Israel praised Absalom for being a very handsome man. He did not seem to have any flaws in any part of his body. His hair was long, thick, and heavy.
How long did Absalom live in Jerusalem without seeing the king’s face?
Absalom lived in Jerusalem for two years, during which David still did not allow Absalom to come and speak with him.
What did Absalom tell his servants to do after Joab refused to come to him?
Absalom told his servants to go and burn Joab’s barley field with fire.
What did Absalom want Joab to do?
Absalom wanted Joab to go to the king and ask why he had come from Geshur, and to say that he wanted to come and speak with him.
What did the king do when Absalom bowed before him?
The king kissed Absalom on the cheek to show that he was no longer hostile to him.
What did Absalom prepare for himself?
Absalom prepared a chariot and horses for himself.
He hired fifty men to run in front of his chariot.
Whom would Absalom call to as he stood by the gate?
Absalom would call to any man who had a dispute and was coming to the king for judgment.
What would Absalom say about the cases of the men who came for judgment?
Absalom would say to them that their matter was good and right, but the king is not able to decide everyone’s case, and he has not appointed anyone else to judge cases for people like you.
Why did Absalom say he wished he were a judge in the land?
Absalom said he wished he were a judge so that every person with a dispute could come to him and he would give them justice.
What did Absalom do when a man approached to prostrate himself?
Absalom would stretch out his hand, hold the man up, and kiss him on the cheek.
What did Absalom steal from the men of Israel?
Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel. The Israelites began to wish that Absalom were their king instead of David.
What reason did Absalom give the king for needing to go to Hebron?
Absalom said he had to go to Hebron to fulfill a vow he had made to Yahweh.
What did the spies that Absalom sent throughout Israel say?
The spies said that when people heard the sound of the shofar, they should say that Absalom has become the king at Hebron.
Did the two hundred men who went with Absalom to Hebron know of his plans?
No, the two hundred men came because he had invited them to the feast he was going to host there. They were not part of his conspiracy. They knew nothing about what he was planning to do.
What did David tell his servants to do after a messenger told him that the hearts of the men of Israel were behind Absalom?
David told his servants in Jerusalem to arise and flee, because there would be no escape from Absalom.
Whom did the king leave behind in Jerusalem to keep the house?
The king left ten women, who were concubines, to keep the house.
Who marched with the king as he left Jerusalem?
All his servants, all the Cherethites, all the Pelethites, and all the Gittites—600 men from Gath—marched with him.
What did Ittai the Gittite tell the king after the king told him to return?
Ittai swore that he would go wherever the king would go, and he would fight to defend David even if he had to die doing that.
Which way did David and all those with him go as they left Jerusalem?
Since Absalom would be coming from the southwest, the king and the others crossed the Kidron Valley and then went up the hill on the road that goes through the desolate area east of Jerusalem.
What did the king tell Zadok the priest to do with the Box of God?
The king told Zadok to take the Box of God back to the city.
Why was David going to wait at the fords of the wilderness?
He was going to wait there until a word came from the priests to tell him what to do.
What did David pray when he was told that Ahithophel was with Absalom?
David prayed that Yahweh would make Ahithophel give Absalom bad advice.
Who did David meet at the top of the Mount of Olives?
David unexpectedly met Hushai the Archite, who had torn his clothes and put dirt on his head to show that he was very sad.
What did David want Hushai the Archite to do for him?
David wanted Hushai to return to the city and offer to be Absalom’s servant so he would be able to counter any good advice that Ahithophel would give to Absalom.
To whom did David want Hushai to report everything he heard in the king’s palace?
David wanted Hushai to report everything to Zadok and Abiathar the priests.
What did Ziba, the servant of Mephibosheth, bring to David?
Ziba brought a pair of saddled donkeys, 200 loaves of bread, 100 clusters of raisins, 100 summer fruits, and a skin of wine.
According to Ziba, why did Mephibosheth stay in Jerusalem?
Ziba said Mephibosheth stayed because he said that the house of Israel would return the kingdom of his father to him that day.
What did the king say now belonged to Ziba?
The king told Ziba that all that belonged to Mephibosheth was now his.
What did Shimei do to David and all the king’s officials?
Shimei came out cursing, and he threw stones at David and all the servants of King David.
Shimei called David a man of blood and a man of wickedness.
What did David hope Yahweh would do in response to Shimei’s cursing?
David hoped that Yahweh would look at his affliction and return good to him in place of the cursing.
When Absalom came to Jerusalem, what did Hushai say to him?
Hushai said to Absalom, “May the king live! May the king live!”
To whom did Hushai tell Absalom he would belong?
Hushai told Absalom that he would belong to the one whom Yahweh, the people, and every man of Israel had chosen.
What did Ahithophel advise Absalom to do?
Ahithophel advised Absalom to go in to his father’s concubines whom David had left to keep the house.
The counsel of Ahithophel was viewed as if God himself had recommended it.
What did Ahithophel advise Absalom and all the elders of Israel about how he should attack David?

Ahithophel’s advice was to let him lead a large army carry out a surprise attack on David that night, when he was weary and weak, kill only David, and bring back all the rest of the people for Absalom to rule.
What was Hushai’s opinion of Ahithophel’s plan?
Hushai said that the counsel Ahithophel had given on this occasion was not good.
Why did Hushai say the plan was not good?

Hushai said that David and his very brave warriors were probably in a safe place, and David’s soldiers will certainly kill some of Ahithophel’s soldiers at the start of the battle. When people hear about that, they will say that David’s soldiers are slaughtering Absalom’s soldiers! Then your other soldiers, even if they are as fearless as lions, will become very afraid.
What did Hushai advise Absalom to do?

Hushai advised Absalom to gather all of Israel, from Dan to Beersheba, and for Absalom himself to go into the battle. He said that this great army would overwhelm David’s smaller army and none of them would survive.
How did Absalom and the men of Israel respond to Hushai’s advice?
They said the counsel of Hushai was better than the counsel of Ahithophel and they decided to do what Hushai suggested.
What message did Hushai send to David?

The message was that David should not stay at the place where people can walk across the Jordan River but should cross over immediately, because otherwise, Absalom and his army may come and kill them.
How was information relayed to King David?
A maidservant of the two priests would go and declare news to Jonathan and Ahimaaz, and they would go and declare it to King David.
What did Jonathan and Ahimaaz do when a young man saw them and told Absalom?
The two of them went quickly to the house of a man in Bahurim and went down into a well in his courtyard.
How were the two men helped?
The man’s wife spread a covering over the well and spread grain on it, and when Absalom’s servants asked where the men were, she told them they had crossed the brook.
After Absalom’s men left, what did the two men do?
They came up from the well, went and reported the news to King David, and told him to get all these people across the Jordan River quickly.
What did Ahithophel do when he saw that his counsel was not followed?

Ahithophel saddled his donkey, went to his house, gave to his family instructions about what to do with his possessions, and then he hanged himself because he knew that otherwise David would kill him as a traitor.
How were David and his people cared for in the wilderness?
Shobi, Machir, and Barzillai brought beds, basins, pottery, and all kinds of food for David and the people with him to eat.
What did King David tell the army?
King David told the army that he would also go out with them himself.
What was the response from the men in the army to King David?
The men told King David not to go out, because he was worth ten thousand of them, and it was better for him to be ready to help them from the city.
What instructions did the king give his commanders about Absalom?
The king told the commanders not to harm the young man Absalom for his sake.
What was the outcome of the battle in the Forest of Ephraim?

The people of Israel were struck down before the servants of David, and more of Absalom’s soldiers died because of accidents in the forest than the number of them whom David’s soldiers killed in the battle.
What happened to Absalom when the mule he was riding ran under the thick branches of a large oak tree?
Absalom’s head was caught in the oak tree. The mule kept going, and that left Absalom dangling in the air.
Why was Joab upset with the man who saw Absalom?
Joab was upset because the man did not kill Absalom immediately.
Why did the man refuse to kill Absalom?
He refused because he had heard the king command his commanders to keep from hurting the young man Absalom.
What did Joab do to Absalom?
Joab took three spears and thrust them into the heart of Absalom while he was still alive in the oak tree.
What was done with Absalom’s body?
They threw Absalom’s body into a great pit in the forest and set up a very great heap of stones over him.
Why had Absalom set up a pillar for himself in the Valley of the King while he was alive?
Absalom set up a pillar to make his name remembered, because he said he had no son to make people remember his name.
Why did Joab tell Ahimaaz not to run to the king with the news?
Joab told him not to bring the news that day because the king’s son was dead.
Why did Ahimaaz still run and tell David the news?
Ahimaaz insisted on running after the Cushite, even though Joab told him there was no reward for the news, so Joab told him to go.
What did the king think when the watcher reported a lone runner?
The king said that if the man was by himself, that indicates that he is bringing news.
What did the king think when the watcher reported another lone runner?
The king said that this one was also bringing news.
What did the king think when the watcher identified the first runner as Ahimaaz?
The king said that he was a good man and came with good news.
What news did Ahimaaz bring to the king?
Ahimaaz told the king that Yahweh had defeated the men who had lifted their hand against the king.
How did Ahimaaz answer when the king asked about Absalom?
Ahimaaz said he saw a great tumult but did not know what it was about.
What was the Cushite’s answer when the king asked about Absalom?
The Cushite said that he wished that what happened to Absalom would happen to all of David’s enemies and to anyone who rebels against him.
How did the king respond to the news of his son’s death?
The king trembled, went up to the upper room of the gate, and wept, wishing he had died in place of his son.
Why did the victory that day turn into mourning for all the people?
The victory turned into mourning because the people heard that the king was grieved because of his son.
The king cried, “My son Absalom! Absalom, my son, my son!”
What did Joab say would have pleased the king?
Joab said that he could see that if Absalom were still alive and all of David’s men were dead today, David would like that better.
What did Joab tell the king would happen if he did not go out and speak to his servants?
Joab swore by Yahweh that if the king did not go out, all his soldiers will have abandoned him by tomorrow morning.
When did all the people come before the king?
All the people came before the king after they were told that the king was sitting in the gate.
What were the people in the tribes of Israel arguing about?
The people were arguing about what they should do now that Absalom was dead and David had left Israel to escape from Absalom.
Whom did King David send to speak to the elders of Judah?
David sent Zadok and Abiathar the priests to speak to the elders of Judah.
Whom did David say would be the commander of his army in place of Joab?
David said Amasa would be the commander of the army in place of Joab.
Why did the men of Judah come to Gilgal?
The men of Judah came to Gilgal to meet the king and to bring him across the Jordan.
Who rushed to the Jordan to meet the king?
Shimei, with 1,000 men from Benjamin, and Ziba, with his 15 sons and 20 servants, rushed to the Jordan.
Why did Shimei say he was the first from the house of Joseph to meet the king?
Shimei came first because he knew that he had sinned against the king.
What did the king say to Shimei after Abishai said Shimei should be put to death?
The king told Shimei that he would not die, and he swore an oath to him.
How did Mephibosheth look when he came to meet the king?
Mephibosheth had not cared for his feet, trimmed his mustache, or washed his clothes from the day the king went away.
What reason did Mephibosheth give for not going with the king?
Mephibosheth told the king that his servant, Ziba, had deceived him and left without him, and Mephibosheth could not follow him because he was crippled.
What else did Mephibosheth say Ziba had done to him?
Mephibosheth said Ziba had lied about him to the king.
How did Mephibosheth reply when the king said he and Ziba should divide the field?
Mephibosheth told the king to let Ziba take the whole field, because all that mattered to him was that the king had returned safely.
What had Barzillai done for the king?
Barzillai had provided all of the food that the king and his soldiers needed while they were at Mahanaim.
Why did Barzillai say he should not go to Jerusalem with the king?
Barzillai said he was too old, could no longer taste what he ate or drank, could not hear singers, and would be a burden to the king.
What did Barzillai request of the king?
Barzillai asked to return to his own city to die, but he asked the king to take his servant Chimham and do for him what was good in the king’s eyes.
Who crossed over to Gilgal with the king?
Chimham, all the people of Judah, and also half the people of Israel crossed over to Gilgal with the king.
Why did the men of Israel say they had more right to David than the men of Judah?

The men of Israel said they had more right to David because they represented ten tribes that were related to the king. The men of Judah represented only one tribe. Also, the people of Judah had started the rebellion against David.
Whose words were harsher, the men of Judah or the men of Israel?
The word of the men of Judah was harsher than the word of the men of Israel.
Why was Sheba called a man of wickedness?
He was called a man of wickedness because he blew a shofar and told the men of Israel to return home; he said David did not belong to them at all.
How was the response of the men of Judah to Sheba different from the men of Israel?
The men of Judah clung to their king, but the men of Israel did what Sheba had said and returned to their homes.
How did David’s relationship with his ten concubines change?
He put them in another residence where someone guarded them. They had to stay in that house until they died. David provided what they needed, but he never had sexual relations with them again.
What did the king tell Amasa to do?
The king told Amasa to call up the men of Judah within three days and to be there himself.
How did David respond when Amasa was delayed?

David told Abishai to take the soldiers already here and go to capture him. If not, we will no longer know where his is going, and the delay would allow him and his soldiers to go into fortified cities.
What did Joab do when he greeted Amasa?
As Joab held Amasa’s beard with his right hand to kiss him, he struck him in the stomach with the sword in his left hand.
What did one of Joab’s men do after Joab stabbed Amasa?
He stood by Amasa and called for those who delighted in Joab and David to follow Joab, and then he removed Amasa’s body from the road into a field so the soldiers would not stop to look.
What did Joab and his men do when they found Sheba in Abel Beth Maacah?
They besieged him in the city built a dirt ramp up against the outer wall of the city to batter and collapse the city wall.
How did the wise woman describe the residents of her city of Abel to Joab?
She described the residents as peaceful and loyal Israelites.
What did the woman ask Joab?
The woman asked Joab why he would try to destroy an Israelite community.
What condition did Joab give the woman for withdrawing from the city?
Joab said that if they would give him Sheba, who is rebelling against King David, he would go away from the city.
How did the people of the city respond to Joab’s condition?
The woman came to the people in her wisdom, and they cut off the head of Sheba and threw it to Joab.
Adoniram was over the forced labor.
Why was there a famine in the land for three years?

There was a famine because of the bloodguilt on Saul and his house. The Israelites had solemnly promised that they would not kill them, but Saul had tried to kill all of them because he wanted the people of Judah and Israel to be the only ones living in that land.
Why did King David want to make atonement to the Gibeonites?
David wanted to make atonement so that they ask Yahweh to do good things for us Israelites again.
What did David agree to do to atone for the injustice done to the Gibeonites?
David agreed to do whatever the Gibeonites asked him to do.
What did the Gibeonites request from David to atone for Saul’s actions?
They requested that seven men from Saul’s sons be given to them so they could hang them before Yahweh at Gibeah.
How did David respond to the Gibeonites’ request?
David spared Mephibosheth but gave them the two sons of Rizpah and the five sons of Michal, and the Gibeonites hanged them on the hill.
What did Rizpah do to express her grief for her sons?

She did not allow any birds to come near the corpses during the day, and she did not allow any animals to come near them during the night from the time that people started to harvest barley until the autumn rains began.
From whom did David take the bones of Saul and Jonathan?
David took the bones of Saul and Jonathan from the leaders of the city of Jabesh Gilead.
How did Abishai rescue David when he was weary?
When David was weary, Abishai helped him by striking and killing the Philistine giant Ishbi Benob, who had intended to kill David.
Why did David’s men insist that he no longer go into battle with them?
They said that if enemy soldiers killed him in battle, Israel would no longer have him as king to guide them.
Whom did David and his servants kill in Gath?
They killed four giants who were born to Rapha in Gath.
When did David sing the song that Yahweh was his rock?
David sang the song on the day Yahweh delivered him from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul.
When David calls on Yahweh, what does he say that Yahweh does?
David says when he calls on Yahweh, he is saved from his enemies.
What did David feel like when he was surrounded by his enemies?
David felt like the waves of death and the cords of Sheol surrounded him.
How did David respond to his distressing circumstances?
In his distress, David called to Yahweh, and Yahweh heard his voice from his temple.
What happened because God was angry?
The earth shook and trembled, smoke went up from his nose, and a stream of fire was flowing out from his mouth to burn up everything in its path.
How did Yahweh come down from the heavens?
He lowered the heavens and came down, riding on a cherub and flying on the wings of the wind.
How did Yahweh scatter his enemies?
Yahweh thundered from the heavens, sent out arrows and flashes of lightning, and panicked them.
How were the foundations of the world uncovered?
The foundations of the world were uncovered at the rebuke of Yahweh, from the blast of the breath of his nose.
How did Yahweh rescue David from the strong enemy who hated him?
David said it was as if Yahweh reached down from heaven and grabbed him so that he could pull David up out of the deep water of the ocean.
Yahweh delivered David because he delighted in him.
How did David keep the ways of Yahweh?
David kept the ways of Yahweh and did not turn away from his statutes.
What happened because David was blameless and kept himself from iniquity?
Yahweh gave back to him according to his righteousness and his cleanness.
What does Yahweh do to the proud?
Yahweh is aware of people who are arrogant, and he humiliates them.
What is Yahweh to everyone who takes refuge in him?
Yahweh is a shield to all who take refuge in him.
Why did David say God was his rock and fortress?

David said God was his rock, the only real God, because God is where he can go to be safe. He said God was his fortress of strength because, to David, God is like a very secure place where he could go to hide from danger.
Why had David’s feet not slipped?
David says that God gave him many ways to respond to each situation, so that his enemies were not able to trap him.
What did David do to his enemies when they looked for a savior?
David defeated them so completely that they were no longer any threat to him no more than tiny particles of dust would be.
What did Yahweh do for David?
Yahweh rescued David from the disputes of his people and kept him as the head of nations.
What did Yahweh do on behalf of David?
Yahweh enabled David to conquer enemies, protecting him from being captured by them. Yahweh kept David safe when people rebelled against him and rescued hm from men who tried to harm him.
Why did David sing praises to the name of Yahweh?

David said he thanks Yahweh so that all people groups will know that Yahweh is the one who has helped him. He sings to praise Yahweh for the great things he has done, faithfully showing kindness to David and to his descendants in the future.
What are the last words of David said to be?
They are the oracle of David, the man raised to a high position, the anointed of the God of Jacob, and the one who wrote beautiful songs for the people of Israel.
What did the God of Israel say to David?
The God of Israel said that a righteous one ruling over man in the fear of God is like the light of morning when the sun rises.
Why will the wicked be like a thorn thrown away?
God will remove people who disrespect him, just as people throw away thorns that hurt their hands when they try to pick them up.
How did Eleazar defeat the Philistines?

When other Israelites retreated in fear, Eleazar arose and struck the Philistines until his hand cramped and he could not let go of his sword, Yahweh won a great victory for the Israelites on that day.
What did Shammah defend against the Philistines?

When other Israelite soldiers ran away from the battle, Shammah stationed himself in the middle of the field full of ripe lentils and fought and killed the Philistines, who wanted to steal the lentils. And so Yahweh won a great victory for the Israelites.
What did the three mighty warriors do when they heard David express his desire for water from the well of Bethlehem?
The three warriors broke through the camp of the Philistines, drew water from the well, and brought it to David.
Why did David refuse to drink the water from the well of Bethlehem?
David said it would not be right to drink it because he said that would be like drinking the blood of these men who were willing to die to get it for him.
He once fought against 300 enemy soldiers and killed them all. As a result, he became famous like the three very greatest soldiers.
How did Benaiah kill a huge Egyptian soldier?
Benaiah went down against the Egyptian with a staff, seized the spear from the Egyptian’s hand, and killed him with his own spear.
What did David ask Joab to do?
David asked Joab to go through all the tribes of Israel and count the men who could fight as soldiers.
Why was Joab reluctant to count the people?
Joab did not understand why David wanted to count the people, and he did not think it was a good idea to count how many soldiers they had.
How long did it take for Joab to go throughout all the land and return to Jerusalem?
It took nine months and twenty days for Joab to go throughout all the land and return to Jerusalem.
How many fighting men did Joab count?
They reported to David that there were 800,000 men in Israel and 500,000 men in Judah who were fit to serve as soldiers in the army.
Why did David feel very badly after he had counted the people?
David realized that he had committed a very serious sin, confessed it to Yahweh, and asked Yahweh to forgive him for his foolish act.
What message did Yahweh give to David through the prophet Gad?
Yahweh told David that he must choose one of three punishments.
What three choices of punishment did God give to David?
God offered a choice of seven years of famine, three months of fleeing from his enemies, or three days of plague in the land.
Why did not more than 70,000 people die in the plague?
Yahweh grieved about punishing any more people, and told the angel to lower his hand.
What did David request of Yahweh when he saw the angel?
David said that he had sinned, and he asked that Yahweh’s hand be against him and his father’s house, not against the people.
What did Gad the prophet tell David to do?
Gad told David to go up and set up an altar for Yahweh on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.
What was David’s purpose for going to Araunah?
David wanted to buy the threshing floor to build an altar for Yahweh so that he will stop the plague that has been killing so many Israelites.
Why did David insist on buying Araunah’s threshing floor for a price?
David insisted on buying it because he would not offer to Yahweh burnt offerings that cost him nothing.
How did David stop the plague in Israel?
David built an altar for Yahweh and he offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. Then Yahweh answered David’s prayers, and he ended the plague that had been killing so many Israelites.
What problem did King David have when he became old?
Although they covered King David with blankets, he could not get warm.
Although Abishag was very beautiful and served the king by caring for him, what did David not do with her?
The king did not have sexual relations with Abishag.
How did Adonijah the son of Haggith exalt himself?
Adonijah wanted to be king, so he prepared for himself chariots and horses and 50 men to run ahead of him.
Did King David discipline his son Adonijah and correct his actions?
No, King David had never rebuked him for anything that he did.
Who were the two men who followed and helped Adonijah?
Joab and Abiathar helped Adonijah in his plot to become king.
Who did Adonijah not invite to his sacrifice?
Adonijah did not invite Nathan the prophet, Benaiah, the mighty men, or his brother Solomon.
Who warned Bathsheba the mother of Solomon that Adonijah had become king and that her life was in danger?
Nathan the prophet warned Bathsheba that her life and the life of her son Solomon were both in danger.
What questions did Nathan tell Bathsheba to ask King David?
Nathan the prophet told Bathsheba to ask David whether he promised her that Solomon would be king and to ask why Adonijah is trying to be the next king.
What promise had King David sworn to Bathsheba?
David had sworn to Bathsheba that her son Solomon would be king after David died.
What did Bathsheba tell King David that Adonijah had done?
Bathsheba told him that Adonijah had become king without David knowing it, and that he had sacrificed animals in abundance.
What did Bathsheba fear would happen when David died?
She feared that she and her son Solomon would be regarded as if we had done something wrong.
Why did Nathan the prophet come to visit King David?
Nathan the prophet came to inform King David that Adonijah was setting himself up as king without David’s knowledge.
What question did Nathan the prophet ask of King David?
Nathan asked him if David had said that Adonijah would reign after him and sit on his throne as king.
What oath did King David make to Bathsheba?
David made an oath that Solomon the son of Bathsheba would reign after him and sit on his throne in David’s place.
What did King David tell Zadok, Nathan, and Benaiah to do for his son Solomon?
King David told his three loyal subjects to take Solomon to Gihon on David’s own mule and to anoint him as king over Israel.
How did the people respond when Zadok anointed Solomon as king?
The people said “Long live King Solomon!” and rejoiced loudly.
What did Adonijah do when he heard the news that David had made Solomon the king of Israel?
Adonijah was afraid of Solomon, and went into the temple of God and took hold of the horns of the altar.
What did King Solomon tell Adonijah to do when they brought him before Solomon?
King Solomon told Adonijah to go to his house.
What did King David tell his son Solomon?
David told his son to obey everything that God directed and instructed them to do.
What was Yahweh’s promise to David?
Yahweh promised that David would never cease to have a descendant on Israel’s throne.

What happened to Jeroboam’s hand when he reached out from the altar?
When Jeroboam reached out from the altar, his hand was dried up so he could not draw it back to himself.
The altar was split apart and the ashes poured out, just as the man of God described.
What happened when the man of God prayed to Yahweh about Jeroboam’s hand?
When the man of God prayed to Yahweh, the king’s hand was restored and became as it was before.
What did the king say to the man of God?
The king said to the man of God, “Come home with me, and I will give you a reward.”
What did the man of God say to the king?
The man of God said to the king, “I will not go with you.”
What did the man of God do after speaking with the king?
After speaking with the king, the man of God returned home by a different way than he came to Bethel.
Where did an old prophet live?
An old prophet lived in Bethel.
Who saw the way that the man of God had gone from Bethel?
The old prophet’s sons saw the way that the man of God walked who had come from Judah.
Where did the old prophet find the man of God?
The old prophet found the man of God sitting under the oak tree.
What did the old prophet say to the man of God?
The old prophet said to the man of God, “Come home with me and eat food.”
What was the man of God’s answer to the old prophet?
The man of God answered, “I am not allowed to go with you into your house, or to eat or drink anything with you.”
What was the old prophet’s answer to the man of God?
The old prophet was lying to the man of God when he told him that an angel told the old prophet to bring him back to your house.
Where did the man of God go after the old prophet lied to him?
The man of God went back and ate food and drank water in his house.
What came to the old prophet as they sat at the table?
The word of Yahweh came to the old prophet as they sat at the table.
What did the word of Yahweh say to the man of God?
The word of Yahweh said, “Because you came back and ate food and drank water, your body will not be buried in the tomb of your fathers.”
What did the old prophet do after they ate?
After they ate, the old prophet saddled the man of God’s donkey for him.
What happened after the man of God had gone?
After the man of God had gone, a lion met him on the road and killed him.
What did men do when they saw the body of the man of God lying on the road?
When men saw the man of God’s body lying on the road, they came back and told it in the city of the old prophet.
What was the old prophet’s answer to the men?
The old prophet answered that this was the man of God who had disobeyed the word of Yahweh.
What did the old prophet do after hearing the men?
The old prophet spoke to his sons to saddle his donkey, and he went and found the body left in the road.
What did the old prophet do with the body of the man of God?
The old prophet took up the body of the man of God and buried him in his own grave.
What did the old prophet say to his sons about his own burial?
The old prophet said to his sons, “When I am dead, bury me in the tomb in which the man of God is buried.”
What thing became sin to the family of Jeroboam and caused it to be cut off from the face of the earth?
Jeroboam did not turn away from evil, and even more, he consecrated as priests anyone who wanted to be a priest.
What happened to Abijah the son of Jeroboam?
Abijah the son of Jeroboam fell sick.
What did Jeroboam ask his wife to do?
Jeroboam asked his wife to disguise herself and go to the prophet Ahijah in Shiloh.
Why did Jeroboam ask his wife to go to the prophet Ahijah?
Jeroboam asked his wife to go to the prophet Ahijah to find out what would happen to his sick son.
What was wrong with Ahijah’s eyes?
Since Ahijah was old, he was blind and his eyes could not see.
Who told Ahijah, “The wife of Jeroboam is coming to see you.”?
Yahweh told Ahijah, “The wife of Jeroboam is coming to see you to seek advice concerning her son.”
What did Ahijah say to the wife of Jeroboam?
When Ahijah heard her come in at the door he said to her, “I know you are Jeroboam’s wife, so do not pretend that you are someone else.”
What did the God of Israel say about Jeroboam?
The God of Israel said to Jeroboam, “You are not like my servant David, who kept my commandments.”
What did Jeroboam do to provoke Yahweh to anger?
Jeroboam cast metal images to provoke Yahweh to anger.
What disaster would Yahweh bring on Jeroboam?
Yahweh said that he would cut off from him every male of his household, whether they are family members or servants, whether they are young or old.
What would happen to anyone of Jeroboam’s family who died in the city?
Any of Jeroboam’s family who died in the city would be eaten by dogs.
What would all Israel do for the child of Jeroboam?
All Israel would mourn for and bury the child of Jeroboam.
What did Yahweh say that Jeroboam led Israel to do?
Yahweh said that Jeroboam led Israel to worship statues of the goddess Asherah, as he was doing.
How far did Yahweh say that he would scatter Israel?
Yahweh said that he would scatter Israel beyond the Euphrates River.
What happened when Jeroboam’s wife came to the threshold of the house?
When Jeroboam’s wife came to the threshold of the house, the child died.
What did all Israel do after the child died?
All Israel buried him and mourned for him.
Where were the other matters concerning Jeroboam written?
The other matters concerning Jeroboam were written in the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel.
How many years did Jeroboam reign before he slept with his fathers?
Jeroboam reigned for 22 years, and he slept with his fathers.
Rehoboam the son of Solomon was reigning in Judah.
How did Judah provoke Yahweh to jealousy?
Judah provoked Yahweh to jealousy with the sins they committed.
What did Judah build on every high hill and under every green tree?
Judah built shrines and Asherah poles on every high hill and under every green tree.
What despicable things did the nations do?
The Israelite people did the same disgraceful things with male prostitutes that the people had done whom Yahweh had forced to leave so that the Israelites could possess the land.
In what year did Shishak come up against Jerusalem?
In the fifth year of King Rehoboam, Shishak came up against Jerusalem.
What shields did Shishak take away from Jerusalem?
Shishak took all the shields of gold that Solomon had made.
What did King Rehoboam do with the shields of bronze that he made?
King Rehoboam put them into the hands of the palace guards.
When would the guards carry the shields of bronze?
Whenever the king entered the house of Yahweh, the guards would carry the shields.
Where were the other matters of King Rehoboam written?
The other matters of King Rehoboam were written in book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah.
Who became king in Rehoboam’s place?
Abijah, Rehoboam’s son, became king in his place.
When did Abijah begin to reign over Judah?
Abijah began to reign over Judah in the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam.
How long did Abijah rule in Jerusalem?
Abijah ruled in Jerusalem for three years.
Was Abijah’s heart devoted to Yahweh his God?
Abijah’s heart was not devoted to Yahweh his God.
Why did Yahweh raise up a son for Abijah in Jerusalem?
Yahweh raised up a son for Abijah for the sake of David.
In what matter did David turn away from Yahweh?
David only turned away from Yahweh in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.
What happened all the days of Abijah’s life?
There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all the days of Abijah’s life.
When Abijah slept with his fathers, who became king in his place?
When Abijah slept with his fathers, Asa became king in his place.
When did Asa begin to reign over Judah?
Asa began to reign over Judah in the twentieth year of Jeroboam king of Israel.
How many years did Asa reign in Jerusalem?
What did Asa do in the eyes of Yahweh?
Asa did what was right in the eyes of Yahweh, as David had done.
What did Asa do in the land?
Asa removed the male prostitutes and the idols his ancestors had made in the land.
Whom did Asa remove from being queen?
Asa removed his own grandmother Maacah from being queen.
What was the condition of Asa’s heart toward Yahweh?
Asa’s heart was completely dedicated to Yahweh all his days.
What did Asa bring into the house of Yahweh?
Asa brought all the items that his father had dedicated to God and all the gold and silver things that he had dedicated to God into the house of Yahweh.
With whom was Asa at war?
Asa was at war with Baasha king of Israel all their days.
Why did Baasha build up Ramah?
Baasha built up Ramah so that no one would enter into or leave the area that King Asa ruled.
What did Asa do with all the silver and gold from the storerooms of the house of Yahweh?
Asa sent the silver and gold to Ben Hadad, the grandson of the king of Aram, who lived in Damascus.
What did Asa say to Benhadad?
Asa said to Benhadad, “Let there be a treaty between me and you, as there was between my father and your father.”
What did Benhadad do after he listened to Asa?
After he listened to Asa, Benhadad sent his armies to attack the cities of Israel.
What did Baasha do when he heard about this?
When Baasha heard about the attacks, he stopped building up Ramah.
What did Asa do with the materials that had been used to build up Ramah?
Asa took the materials that had been used to build up Ramah and used them to build up Geba and Mizpah.
Where were all of Asa’s matters written?
All of Asa’s matters were written in the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah.
After Asa slept with his fathers, who became king in his place?
After Asa slept with his fathers, his son Jehoshaphat became king in his place.
Who began to reign over Israel in the second year of Asa?
Nadab the son of Jeroboam began to reign over Israel in the second year of Asa.
How did Nadab walk in the sight of Yahweh?
Nadab did evil in the sight of Yahweh and walked in the ways of his father and in his sin.
What did Baasha son of Ahijah do at Gibbethon?
Baasha the son of Ahijah killed Nadab at Gibbethon.
What did Baasha do as soon as he became king?
As soon as Baasha became king, he killed all of the family of Jeroboam. He did not leave one of Jeroboam’s descendants breathing.
How long was there war between Asa and Baasha?
There was war between Asa and Baasha all their days.
How long did Baasha reign in Tirza?
Baasha reigned in Tirza for 24 years.
Baasha did evil in the sight of Yahweh and lived in the way of Jeroboam. encouraging his people to sin in the same way that he sinned.
Out of what did Yahweh raise Baasha?
Yahweh raised him out of the dust.
What would eat anyone belonging to Baasha who died in the city?
The dogs would eat anyone belonging to Baasha who died in the city.
Why did the word of Yahweh come against Baasha and his family?
The word of Yahweh came against Baasha and his family both because of all the evil he did in the sight of Yahweh and also because he had killed all of Jeroboam’s family.
What was Elah doing when Zimri killed him?
Elah was drinking himself drunk in the house of Arza when Zimri killed him.
When did Zimri kill all the family of Baasha?
When Zimri began to reign, as soon as he had sat on his throne, he killed all the family of Baasha.
Zimri killed himself in the citadel attached to the king’s palace, burning it down over himself and dying in the fire.
About what two leaders were the people of Israel divided into two parts?
The people of Israel divided into two parts about who should be their king, Tibni or Omri.
Why did Omri call the name of the city Samaria?
Omri called the name of the city Samaria, after the name of Shemer, the owner of the hill.
Who became king in Omri’s place?
Ahab his son became king in his place.
Who had built the house of Baal in Samaria?
Ahab had built the house of Baal in Samaria.
What caused the loss of Hiel’s son Abiram?
Hiel began rebuilding Jericho, causing the loss of his oldest son, Abiram.
What ominous message did Elijah give to Ahab?
Elijah told Ahab that as Yahweh lives, there would be no dew or rain unless he said so.
Who did Yahweh command to feed Elijah while Elijah was at the brook Cherith?
Yahweh commanded the ravens to feed Elijah at the brook Cherith.
What happened when there was no rain in the land?
The brook dried up when there was no rain in the land.
Where did Elijah go after the brook dried up?
Yahweh sent Elijah to a widow in Zarephath.
Why was the widow gathering two sticks?
The widow was gathering two sticks so she could go in and cook for herself and her son, that they could eat, and die from hunger.
For how long would the widow’s jar of meal and jug of oil be full?
They would be full until the day that Yahweh sent rain on the earth.
How sick was the woman’s son?
The son’s sickness was so severe that there was no more breath left in him.
What did Elijah do to save the child?
Elijah stretched himself on the child three times; he cried out to Yahweh and said, “Yahweh my God, please let this child become alive again.”
How did the woman know that Elijah was a man of God?
The woman knew that Elijah was a man of God when her son revived, and Elijah took the child and gave him to his mother.
What message did Yahweh ask Elijah to give to Ahab during the severe famine?
Yahweh asked Elijah to tell Ahab he would send rain on the land.
How did Obadiah honor Yahweh when Jezebel was killing the prophets of Yahweh?
Obadiah honored Yahweh by hiding 100 prophets by fifties in a cave and feeding them with bread and water.
Why did Ahab and Obadiah go through the land to all the water springs and brooks?
Ahab and Obadiah were searching for water and grass so they could keep a horse or a mule alive.
What dangerous message did Elijah ask Obadiah to tell Ahab?
Elijah asked Obadiah to tell Ahab that Elijah is here.
Why was Obadiah reluctant to tell Ahab that “Elijah is here.”?
Obadiah was reluctant to tell Ahab, “Elijah is here,” because all the nearby nations had taken an oath swearing that Elijah was not there.
What did Obadiah think would happen as soon as he left Elijah?
Obadiah thought the Spirit of Yahweh would carry Elijah some place Obadiah would not know.
What did Elijah tell Obadiah to calm his fears?
Elijah told Obadiah that as Yahweh lives, he would surely show himself to Ahab that day.
What did Ahab call Elijah when he met him?
Ahab called Elijah “one troubling Israel” when he met him.
How did Elijah respond to Ahab calling him a “troublemaker”?
Elijah told the king that Ahab and his father’s family were the troublemakers because they abandoned the commandments of Yahweh to follow the Baals.
Who did Elijah say to gather on Mount Carmel?
Elijah said to gather all the people of Israel, along with the 450 prophets of Baal and the four hundred prophets of Asherah who eat at Jezebel’s table.
Who did Elijah tell the people they should follow?
Elijah told the people to follow Yahweh if he was God or follow Baal if he was truly God.
What proposal did Elijah bring before the people?
Elijah proposed that he and the prophets of Baal each call upon their god to consume the sacrifice of a bull by fire to prove which one was God.
How long did the prophets of Baal call on Baal?
The prophets of Baal called on Baal from morning until noon.
After Elijah mocked the prophets of Baal at noon, what did the prophets of Baal do?
The prophets of Baal cried more loudly and cut themselves with swords and spears.
How long did the prophets of Baal continue their raving?
The prophets of Baal were raving until the time of the evening sacrifice.
What did Elijah do to the ruined altar of Yahweh?
Elijah repaired the altar of Yahweh with twelve stones.
What did Elijah make around the altar of Yahweh?
Elijah dug a trench around the altar of Yahweh.
What did Elijah have the people do to the wood and the bull for the burnt offering?
Three times Elijah had the people fill four jars with water and pour them on the burnt offering and the wood.
How did the people of Israel respond when the fire of Yahweh fell and consumed the sacrifice and everything around it?
The people lay face down on the ground and said, “Yahweh, he is God! Yahweh, he is God!”
What did Elijah do with the prophets of Baal?
Elijah brought the prophets of Baal down to the brook of Kishon and killed them.
What did the servant of Elijah see after he looked toward the sea seven times?
On the seventh time, the servant saw a cloud as small as a man’s hand.
What did Elijah tell his servant to say to Ahab?
Elijah told his servant to tell Ahab to make ready his chariot and go down so the rain would not stop him.
What did Elijah do as Ahab rode and went to Jezreel?
Elijah tucked his robe in his belt and ran before Ahab to the entrance of Jezreel.
What threat did Jezebel make to Elijah?
Jezebel told Elijah that by the next day she would have killed him, just like he killed all those prophets of Baal.
How did Elijah respond to the threat from Jezebel?
Elijah fled for his life to Beersheba.
Why did Elijah request that he might die?
Elijah requested that he might die because he felt he was no better than his dead ancestors.
What happened as Elijah was sleeping under a juniper tree?
An angel touched Elijah and said to him, “Get up and eat.”
What did Elijah see and do after the angel touched him?
Elijah saw bread that had been baked on coals and a jug of water. Elijah ate and drank, and then he lay down again.
How long did it take Elijah to get to Horeb, the mountain of God?
Elijah traveled 40 days and 40 nights to Horeb.
How did Elijah respond when Yahweh asked him what he was doing in a cave?

Elijah told Yahweh that he had been very zealous for him, but the people of Israel had forsaken his covenant, destroyed his altars, and killed his prophets, and he was the only one left, and they sought to kill him too.
What did Yahweh tell Elijah to do?
Yahweh told Elijah to return to the wilderness near Damascus to anoint Hazael to be king over Aram, Jehu to be king over Israel, and Elisha to be a prophet in his place.
How did Yahweh respond to Elijah’s claim that he was the only prophet left in the land?
Yahweh told Elijah there were 7,000 people in Israel who never worshiped Baal.
What excuse did Elisha give to Elijah after he draped his cloak on him?
Elisha asked Elijah to let him kiss his mother and father before he followed him.
What was the message which Ahab received from Ben Hadad when the city of Samaria was under siege?
Ben Hadad told Ahab that his silver and gold as well as his wives and children were now Ben Hadad’s possessions.
How did Ben Hadad respond to Ahab’s willingness to give him his silver, gold, wives, and children?
Ben Hadad informed Ahab that he was sending his servants the next day, and they would seize with their hands anything valuable of Ahab’s and bring it to him.
What was the advice which the king of Israel received from all the elders of the land and the people?
